name: uniq
plain: `uniq` finds repeated lines and either removes the repeats, counts them, or shows only the repeated ones. It only compares lines that are next to each other, so you almost always sort first.
uniq -c after sort is the standard way to count how often each thing occurs.
when: Count how many times each IP, user or URL appears.
Remove duplicate lines from a list.
Show only the lines that appear once (or more than once).

examples.title: Count each distinct line  (-c)
examples.explain: sort puts equal lines next to each other, then uniq -c prefixes each distinct line with its count.

examples.title: Rank by count
examples.explain: Adding sort -rn at the end puts the most common value first. This pipeline is worth memorising.

examples.title: Only the duplicates  (-d)
examples.explain: -d prints one copy of each line that occurs more than once.

examples.title: Only the lines that occur once  (-u)
examples.explain: -u prints lines that never repeat: the rare events, which are often the interesting ones.

examples.title: Ignore case  (-i)
examples.explain: Treats upper and lower case as the same when comparing.

examples.title: Compare only part of the line  (-f, -s, -w)
examples.explain: -f N skips the first N fields, -s N skips N characters and -w N compares at most N characters. Useful for lines that start with a timestamp.

options.plain: Prefix lines with the number of occurrences.
Print only the duplicated lines, one per group.
Print all the duplicated lines; METHOD (none, prepend, separate) controls blank-line separators between groups.
Show all lines, separating groups with an empty line; METHOD is separate, prepend, append or both.

options.use: Lines that start with a changing timestamp.

options.plain: Avoid comparing the first N characters.
Compare no more than N characters of each line.
Lines end with a NUL byte instead of a newline.

mistakes: Forgetting to sort first: uniq removes only adjacent duplicates, so unsorted input leaves duplicates behind.
Reading the count wrongly: the number is in front of the line, padded with spaces.
sort | uniq can be replaced by sort -u when you only want duplicates removed.
